questions.question: Which dance style is incorporated with both the Tandava and Lasya?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manipuri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Manipuri:**

__
 
• **Origin:**

 
 
• This dance form originates from the** northeastern state of Manipur** in India.
 
 
 
• **Features:**
 
 
• It includes both **Tandava and Lasya**, blending vigorous movements (representing Tandava) and soft, graceful movements (representing Lasya).
 
• Known for its devotional themes, Manipuri dances are often performed as an offering to gods, particularly** Lord Krishna and Radha**.
 
• The **male performers usually depict Tandava** through martial and vigorous expressions, while** female performers emphasize Lasya** with soft and elegant movements.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Odissi:**

 
• **Origin:**

 
 
• Odissi is a classical dance form from **Odisha**.
 
 
 
• **Features:**
 
 
• It is characterized by fluid, graceful movements, including **Tribhangi posture **(three bends of the body).
 
• Primarily focuses on **Lasya (feminine, graceful)** and **devotional expression to Lord Jagannath**.
 
 
 
• **Reason Incorrect:** Odissi does not have significant elements of Tandava; it leans more towards Lasya.

**Kathak:**

 
• **Origin:**

 
 
• This dance form is rooted in **North India** and is linked to storytelling traditions.
 
 
 
• **Features:**
 
 
• Kathak emphasizes **intricate footwork, fast spins, and expressive gestures**.
 
• It includes energetic movements but is primarily focused on the **rhythmic **aspect rather than a balance of Tandava and Lasya.
 
 
 
• **Reason Incorrect: **While Kathak has moments of vigor (which may seem like Tandava), it lacks a deliberate and distinct representation of both Tandava and Lasya.

**Bharatanatyam:**

 
• **Origin: **

 
 
• **​**Bharatanatyam hails from **Tamil Nadu **in South India.
 
 
 
• **Features:**
 
 
• Bharatanatyam is a **highly expressive dance** form with distinct **Nritta **(pure dance) and **Abhinaya **(expression).
 
• It primarily showcases Lasya but has elements of Tandava in certain vigorous performances like depicting Lord Shiva's cosmic dance.
 
 
 
• **Reason Incorrect: **Though Bharatanatyam includes Tandava elements, it is not as balanced as Manipuri in integrating both Tandava and Lasya equally

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is associated with the state of Odisha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raja Parba**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raja Parba** is a major festival celebrated in the state of Odisha.
 
• This festival is dedicated to the worship of the Earth Goddess and womanhood.
 
• It is a three-day-long festival marking the onset of the monsoon and the advent of the agricultural year.
 
• The first day is called **Pahili Raja**, the second day is **Mithuna Sankranti**, and the third day is **Bhu Daaha or Basi Raja**.
 
• During these days, women take a break from household work and enjoy various indoor and outdoor games.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Odisha, formerly known as Orissa, is an eastern Indian state on the Bay of Bengal known for its tribal cultures and many ancient Hindu temples.
 
• The state is also famous for its classical dance form, Odissi, and its distinct cuisine.
 
• Other important festivals celebrated in Odisha include **Durga Puja, Rath Yatra, and Makar Sankranti**.
 
• Odisha's capital, Bhubaneswar, is often referred to as the "Temple City" of India.

questions.question: Who was the first Deputy Prime Minister of India?
questions.solution:
__**Sardar Ballabh Bhai Patel **__was the first Deputy Prime Minister of India. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was the **first Deputy Prime Minister** of India. 
 
• He was also the **Home Minister of India. **
 
• He was sworn in on August 15, 1947, the day India gained independence from the British Raj. 
 
• He served in this position until his **death on December 15, 1950.**
 
• **L.K. Advani, Morarji Desai, and Charan Singh** were all deputy prime ministers of India, but they came after Sardar Patel. 
 
• **Morarji Desai** was the second deputy prime minister, serving from **1967 to 1977. **
 
• **Charan Singh** was the third deputy prime minister, serving from **1979 to 1980. **
 
• **L.K. Advani** was the seventh deputy prime minister, serving from **1998 to 2004.**

questions.question: Article 12 of the Indian Constitution provides for ____________.

options.text: Definition of Directive Principles of State Policy

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Definition of 'State'**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Article 12 defines the state in the following manner

In this part, unless the context otherwise requires, "the State" includes the Government and Parliament of India and the Government and the Legislature of each of the States and all local or other authorities within the territory of India or under the control of the Government of India.

The following entities are also included in the concept of "State" under Article 12: Railway Board, Electricity Board, Judiciary, University, State Bank of India (SBI). 

 
• The Supreme Court in the case of Rajasthan Electricity Board v. Mohan Lal laid down the conclusive test for determining the bodies that would come under the ambit of ‘other authorities’.

 
 
• The court held that if an authority has the power to issue directions and any offense against them is punishable by law has the power to make rules that would have statutory effect is an agency or instrumentality of state for carrying out trade or business which otherwise would have been carried out by the state departments, such authorities would come within the purview of ‘other authorities’ and hence would be considered ‘state’.
 
 
 
• In the case of A.R. Antulay v. R.S. Nayak, the Court established that the “State” as per Article 12 of the Indian Constitution will include courts only when they are performing non-judicial functions and not while they are performing their judicial functions.
 
• Therefore, in general case judiciary is not included under the definition of State.
 
• The University of Madras v. Shanta bai AIR 1954 – Supreme Court held that the university formed under Madras Act, falls under the definition of the state. Court laid down the Latin term *EJUSDEM GENERIS* means (of the same kind). It was held that the Preceding government is sovereign, government, and parliament, government, and state legislature and local authorities.
 
• But University as a general does not fall under the definitions of "State". As it will include private universities. And private universities are not state.
 
 
• In Umesh v. V.N. Singh, AIR 1986, the Patna High Court, following the decision of the Supreme Court, has held that the Patna University is "a State".
 
 
 
• The Madras High Court held that SBI is a "State" under Article 12 because it is an instrumentality of the government and has a number of public functions.

questions.question: The concept of “Procedure Established by Law” in the Indian constitution is borrowed from which of the following countries?

• It means that a law has been duly enacted by the competent body following the correct procedure. For example, the procedure mentioned in the constitution.
 
• The Doctrine of Procedure established by law has been taken from the Japanese Constitution.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The Indian constitution came into force on 26th January 1950.
 
• It was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26th November 1949. 
 
• Some provisions of the Constitution pertaining to citizenship, elections, provisional parliament, and temporary and transitional provisions.
 
• And short title contained in Articles 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 60, 324, 366, 367, 379, 380, 388, 391, 392 and 393 came into force on November 26, 1949,.
 
• The remaining provisions (the major part) of the Constitution came into force on January 26, 1950.
 
• This day is referred to in the Constitution as the date of its commencement and is celebrated as Republic Day.
 
• January 26 was specifically chosen as the date of commencement of the Constitution because of its historical importance.
 
• It was on this day in 1930 that Purna Swaraj day was celebrated, following the resolution of the Lahore Session (December 1929) of the INC.

questions.question: According to the constitution of India, which of the following are fundamental for the governance of the country?
questions.solution:
According to the constitution of India, __**Directive principles of state policies**__ are fundamental for the governance of the country. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are part of Part IV of the Constitution of India. 
 
• They are a set of guidelines for the state to follow in order to promote the welfare of the people and create a just and equitable society.
 
• The DPSP are **not enforceable by the courts**, but they are nevertheless fundamental for the governance of the country. 
 
• The state is expected to keep the DPSP in mind when making laws and policies.
 
• The DPSP are divided into two broad categories:
 
 
• **​Socialistic principles:**__
 __
 
• These principles aim to create a society in which everyone has equal opportunities and the fruits of development are shared equitably.
 
• They include directives such as the right to an adequate means of livelihood, equal pay for equal work, and free and compulsory education for all children up to the age of 14.
 
 
 
• **Gandhian principles**__:
 __
 
• These principles emphasize the importance of village self-government, decentralized planning, and protection of the environment.
 
• They include directives such as the organization of village panchayats, the promotion of cottage industries, and the protection of forests and wildlife.
 
 
 
 
 
• The DPSP has been **criticized for being too idealistic **and for not being implemented effectively. 
 
• However, they remain an important part of the Indian Constitution and continue to guide the state in its efforts to create a just and equitable society.

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Here are some of the specific Directive Principles of State Policy:

 
 
• **​**____**Socialistic principles**__:

 
 
• ​Secure a social order in which **justice, social, economic and political,** shall inform all the institutions of national life.
 
• Secure the right to an adequate means of livelihood for all citizens.
 
• Equal pay for equal work for both men and women.
 
• Ensure that the **ownership and control of the material resources **of the community are distributed as best to serve the common good.
 
• Provide free and compulsory education for all children up to the **age of 14 years.**
 
• Take steps to organize village panchayats and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self-government.
 
 
 
• **Liberal-Intellectual Principles:**
 
 
• ​Separate the judiciary from the executive.
 
• **Promulgate a uniform civil code** for the whole country.
 
• Protect and improve the environment and safeguard the forests and wildlife of the country.
 
• Promote international peace and security.
 
• Strive to promote international understanding and **cooperation and encourage the settlement** of international disputes by arbitration.
 
 
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are a valuable part of the Indian Constitution. 
 
• They provide a roadmap for the state to follow in its efforts to create a just and equitable society for all its citizens.

questions.question: Babur wrote Tuzuk - i - Baburi in which of the following language?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Turkish**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **autobiography of Zahiruddin Muhammad Babur,** who established the Mughal empire in India, is titled **Tuzuk-i-Baburi.**
 
• It was written in **Turkish by Babur.**
 
• It was translated into **Persian by Abdur Rahim Khan Khan-i-Khanan,** a Mughal imperial officer and the son of Bairam Khan Khan-i-Khanan.
 
• The Tuzuk-i-Baburi is an accurate portrayal of the** author's world and the people** with whom he had contact.
 
• His candor in writing about his** own successes and failures or faults **profoundly impresses the reader.
 
• He writes in an **easy-to-read, straightforward manner** without any **hypocrisy.** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In the **16th century**, Babur established the **Mughal empire** from his** base in Kabul **after conquering northern India.
 
• Through his **father and mother,** he was related to **Genghis Khan and Timur.**
 
• He received the posthumous name **Firdaws Makani.**
 
• **Humayun, Kamran Mirza, and Hindal Mirza **are his sons.
 
• In Agra, Babur passed away in **1530,** and Humayun took his place.
 
• Babur was initially** laid to rest in Agra,** but he requested that his ashes be** transported to Kabul and reinterred there.**

questions.question: Which of the following is a correct description of the Kumaon Himalayas?

options.text: The Himalayas lying between Indus and Satluj rivers
The Himalayas lying between Satluj and Kali rivers
The Himalayas lying between Kali and Teesta rivers
The Himalayas lying between Teesta and Dihang rivers

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Himalayas lying between Satluj and Kali rivers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kumaun Himalayas** is the west-central section of the Himalayas in northern India, extending 200 miles. 
 
• The range, comprising part of the Siwalik Range in the south and part of the Great Himalayas in the north, lies largely within the state of **Uttarakhand, northwest of Nepal.**
 
• Commonly known as the** 'Lake District',** Nainital is nestled high up in the **Kumaon Himalayas**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The part of the Himalayas lying between Indus and Satluj has been traditionally known as Punjab Himalaya but it is also known regionally as Kashmir and Himachal Himalaya from west to east respectively. 
 
• The Himalayas lying between **Kali and Teesta rivers** are known as **Nepal Himalayas. **
 
• The Himalayas lying between** Teesta and Dihang** **rivers** are known as** Assam Himalayas. **

questions.question: Bon-geet (forest/nature song), is primarily a form of folk song of _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bon-Geet a form of folk song of Assam.**
 
• Bongeets are a category of Assamese folk music, very closely resembling the** '****Bihugeets'.**
 
• Bongeet songs are quite favorable in the Assamese society since ancient times and these songs are mostly romantic songs, are sung by the local youngsters of Assam.
 
• The central idea of Bongeet is to convey the natural grandeur of nature, which includes songs describing the hues of dense** forests, ****birds, flowers, and animals.**
 
• Certain songs of Bongeet express the subtle emotions of** tragedy, anxiety, love, and hatred and are devoid of religious influences.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****

 
• ** ****Indian folk music** is diverse because of India's vast cultural diversity.
 
• The folk song of** Manipur i**s** Thoubal chongba.**
 
• **Jhoori** is a popular form of traditional music in** Himachal Pradesh.**

questions.question: In animals like sponges and hydra, transport of food and oxygen is done by ___________.
questions.solution:
In animals like sponges and hydra, transport of food and oxygen is done by water only.

Animals such as sponges and Hydra do not have a circulatory system. The water they live in provides food and oxygen to their bodies.

Water carries waste materials and carbon dioxide as it passes out. Thus these species do not require a blood-like circulatory fluid.

Sponges live mainly in seawater, while hydra lives in freshwater.

Sponges and hydra do not have lungs, blood or heart.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• Transport is a life process in which the substance consumed by one portion of the body of the organism is transferred to other parts of the body.
 
• Amoeba and paramecium are both small creatures that live in water and have no blood in them.

questions.question: What is the IUPAC name of allylamine which is used to make pharmaceuticals and other chemicals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2-Propen-1-amine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Allylamine**:-

 
 
• It is a primary amine with the chemical formula C₃H₅NH2.
 
• It is a colorless liquid with a pungent odor and is highly soluble in water.
 
• Allylamine is used in the production of a wide range of pharmaceuticals, including antihistamines, antifungal agents, and anticancer drugs.
 
• It is also used in the manufacture of various chemicals, including pesticides, resins, and plastics.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Propan-1-amine:-**

 
 
• It refers to a different compound with a different molecular structure.
 
 
 
• **Benzenamine:-**
 
 
• It refers to an entirely different compound with a benzene ring in its structure.
 
 
 
• **N-Methylethanamine:-**
 
 
• It refers to a compound with a different molecular formula and structure.

questions.question: Which of the following nutrient is essential for germination of seeds and used for formation of fruit and nut?
questions.solution:
**__Magnesium__** is essential for the **germination of seeds** and used for** the formation of fruit and nut**.

 
 

 
 
**Magnesium**

 
 
 
**Micro-nutrient**

 
 
 
 
• The structural component of chlorophyll.
 
• Required for the functioning of enzymes to produce carbohydrates, sugar and fats.
 
• Essential for germination of seeds and used for the formation of fruit and nut.
 
 
 
 

 
 
**Potassium**

 
 
 
**Macro-nutrient**

 
 
 
 
• For the **formation of sugar, carbohydrates, protein synthesis and division of the cell in roots**.
 
• Maintains **cation anion balance**.
 
 
 
 

 
 
**Nitrogen**

 
 
 
**Macro nutrient**

 
 
 
 
• Major component of **protein, chlorophyll and other enzymes**
 
• It is needed in highest amount**.**
 
• It is absorbed as** ammonium ion, nitrate ion or nitrite ion.**
 
 
 
 

 
 
**Zinc**

 
 
 
**Micro nutrient**

 
 
 
Essential for C**arbohydrate metabolisms, internodal elongation and protein synthesis**.

questions.question: Who is the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnam Malleswari.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Karnam Malleswari** is the **first Indian woman** to win an **Olympic medal**.
 
• She accomplished this feat during the** 2000 Sydney Olympics**, where she won **a bronze medal** in the **women's 69 kg weightlifting **category.
 
• This landmark achievement marked a significant milestone in the history of Indian women participating in international sports events.
 
• Karnam Malleswari's success sent a strong message to Indian women, encouraging them to pursue sports actively and professionally.
 
• Her win paved the way for more Indian women athletes to aim for success in the Olympic Games and has been a source of inspiration to many Indian sportswomen who succeeded her.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mirabai Chanu:**

 
 
• Mirabai Chanu is an accomplished **Indian weightlifter.**
 
• At the **2020 Tokyo Olympics**, she won a **silver medal** in the **Women's 49 kg category**.
 
• This was India's **first medal in the event** and also made her the **second Indian woman weightlifter to win an Olympic medal** after Karnam Malleswari.
 
 
 
• **PV Sindhu:**
 
 
• PV Sindhu is a **professional badminton player **from India.
 
• She made history when she became the** first Indian woman to win a silver **medal in the** 2016 Rio Olympics **in the singles badminton event.
 
• She also clinched a **bronze medal in the Tokyo 2020 Olympics **making her the first Indian woman to win two Olympic medals.
 
 
 
• **Saina Nehwal:**
 
 
• Saina Nehwal is an Indian **professional badminton singles player.**
 
• She was the** first Indian badminton player** to win an Olympic medal, **a bronze**, in the **2012 London Olympics.**
 
• Nehwal has several other accomplishments, including being the first Indian to win the BWF World Championships and the first Indian woman to reach the **World No.1 ranking.**
